newsitem.title: USA: Worthington to build processing plant.
newsitem.headline: Worthington to build processing plant.

text.p: Worthington Industries Inc said on Thursday it planned to build a $150 million flat rolled steel processing facility in Decatur, Alabama.
Sales at the pickling, slitting and cold rolling facility, Worthington's largest such facility to date, were expected to exceed $400 million at capacity, the company said.
Worthington Chairman and Chief Executive Officer John McConnell also said the operation was expected to create over 200 jobs.

The first phase of the project, including pickling and slitting, was scheduled to start up by mid 1998, the company said. The cold rolling mill would begin operating in the first half of 1999, Worthington said.

Worthington said it was extremely optimistic about growth opportunities for its steel processing business in the southeastern United States. It said this region was the fastest growing flat rolled steel market in the United States.

McConnell also said: "The plant will be strategically located adjacent to Trico, a joint venture among LTV (Corp), Sumitomo (Metal Industries Ltd) and British Steel Plc, which we believe will be one of this country's premier steel mini mills."
